correctness.rationale: Discarding the null endpoint 1, write x=t+kd uniquely with 0≤t<d. Residues t<r have m+1 positions and the remaining residues have m, each position carrying measure dt. On odd chains let S contain even positions and B odd positions. A successful distance-d edge from S must enter B, so for any coupling the success mass is at most 1−λ(S)+λ(B). The difference λ(S)−λ(B) is the residue measure of odd chains, r for even m and d−r for odd m. This uses no disintegration or graph assumption about a competing copula. The adjacent-pair swap is a measurable, measure-preserving involution (piecewise translations, with odd tails fixed), inducing an exchangeable coupling with exactly this failure mass. Positive distances have perfect success only at even reciprocals; at an odd reciprocal 1/k with k≥3 the one-sided slopes −(k+1) and k−1 give a strict local minimum with mass 1−1/k. The boundary cases follow from identical variables at d=0 and zero endpoint mass at d=1. Separate finite assignment reproduction checked all 28 grid size/step cases through size 8 by exhaustive permutations and verified the formula and construction for 8,128 cases through size 128, with exact reciprocal checks. This is not the proof for all real d. The uploaded checker was read, not executed.
residual_risks: The event is an exact ordinary interval distance; the theorem neither imposes absolute continuity of the joint law nor asserts uniqueness of optima.
